newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schwarz Pharma sees higher 1997 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Schwarz Pharma sees higher 1997 earnings.

text.p: German drugs group Schwarz Pharma AG said on Tuesday it expected a five percent increase in group sales in 1997, after reporting a 17.5 percent hike in 1996 group sales to 1.195 billion marks.

The group said in a regulatory statement that group net profit in 1996 was 103.8 million marks, a rise of 14.4 percent, while earnings per share by the DVFA analysts' method was 4.49 marks, up 20 percent.
"The clear rise in earnings can be attributed to internal growth, acquisitions and improvements in the cost structure," the group said in the statement.

First-quarter 1997 pre-tax profits were 51.2 million marks, a rise of 9.2 percent on the same period last year. The group said that domestic demand would remain weak in 1997, but that this would be offset by increased foreign demand.
Domestic sales grew 9.4 percent in 1996 to 584.2 million marks, while foreign sales grew 26 percent to 610.8 million, the first time foreign sales have exceeded domestic sales.
"This narrows the group's dependancy on the German market," Schwarz Pharma said. 51.7 percent of foreign sales were in Europe, while 43.9 percent was in the United States.
Schwarz Pharma said it plans to introduce its EDEX (Prostaglandin) drug in the United States and Germany for the treatment of erectile disfunction in 1997.
It plans to introduce FEMPRESS (Moexipril) in Italy and Germany and Moexipril Combination in the United States, both of which are used for treating high blood pressure.
Return on sales in 1996 was 8.7 percent, while return on equity was 24.8 percent.
The outlook for DVFA earnings per share in 1997 was for a rise to 4.90 marks per share by the German DVFA analysts' method. Cash flow also improved by 26.4 percent to 185.6 million marks.
